entities.name: enumerated value with associated value list matching

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism MAY be used to replace the value of a single template field.
requirements.original: Generally, matching mechanisms are used to replace values of single template fields or to replace even the entire contents of a template.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism MAY be used to replace the entire contents of a template.
requirements.original: Generally, matching mechanisms are used to replace values of single template fields or to replace even the entire contents of a template.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism MAY be used in-line, i.e. in an in-line template.
requirements.original: Matching mechanisms may also be used in-line (see clause 15.4).

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism IS classified into one of four groups: specific values, special symbols that can be used instead of values, special symbols that can be used inside values, and special symbols which describe attributes of values.
requirements.original: Matching mechanisms are arranged in four groups: specific values; special symbols that can be used instead of values; special symbols that can be used inside values; special symbols which describe attributes of values.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: Certain matching mechanisms MAY be used in combination with each other.
requirements.original: Some of the mechanisms may be used in combination.

readings: Only the combinations of matching mechanisms explicitly defined in annex B (e.g. length restriction with AnyElementsOrNone, ifpresent with other mechanisms) MAY be used together.
Any matching mechanisms MAY be combined unless a combination is explicitly forbidden.
ambiguity.issue: "Some of the mechanisms" does not state which mechanisms can be combined; the first reading (only combinations defined in annex B) is chosen because restriction a) forbids all applications not allowed by table 11.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism SHALL NOT be applied to a value or template of a type for which table 11 does not allow it.
requirements.original: a) All other applications of matching mechanisms than the ones allowed in table 11 are forbidden.

requirements.subject: ent:omit
requirements.canonical: `omit` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent
requirements.canonical: `ifpresent` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.

requirements.subject: ent:omit
requirements.canonical: When matching, `omit` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
requirements.original: However when matching, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set types only (without restriction on the type of that field). NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.

readings: `omit` assigned to a whole template SHALL NOT be used in a matching operation (e.g. receive) at all; it may only be applied when matching optional fields of record and set types.
`omit` assigned to a whole template is allowed and only matches optional fields of record and set types when it is used inside such a template.
ambiguity.issue: "it shall be applied ... only" in combination with NOTE 1 allowing assignment to whole templates leaves open whether matching against a whole template containing `omit` is an error or simply never applies; the restriction reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: When matching, AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
requirements.original: However when matching, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set types only (without restriction on the type of that field). NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.

readings: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) assigned to a whole template SHALL NOT be used in a matching operation (e.g. receive) at all; it may only be applied when matching optional fields of record and set types.
AnyValueOrNone (`*`) assigned to a whole template is allowed and only matches optional fields of record and set types when it is used inside such a template.
ambiguity.issue: "it shall be applied ... only" in combination with NOTE 1 allowing assignment to whole templates leaves open whether matching against a whole template containing AnyValueOrNone (`*`) is an error or simply never applies; the restriction reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent
requirements.canonical: When matching, `ifpresent` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
requirements.original: However when matching, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set types only (without restriction on the type of that field). NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.

readings: `ifpresent` assigned to a whole template SHALL NOT be used in a matching operation (e.g. receive) at all; it may only be applied when matching optional fields of record and set types.
`ifpresent` assigned to a whole template is allowed and only matches optional fields of record and set types when it is used inside such a template.
ambiguity.issue: "it shall be applied ... only" in combination with NOTE 1 allowing assignment to whole templates leaves open whether matching against a whole template containing `ifpresent` is an error or simply never applies; the restriction reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: For character string types, AnyElement (`?`) and AnyElementsOrNone (`*`) IS a matching mechanism only within a character pattern.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Have matching mechanism meaning within character patterns only.

requirements.subject: ent:specific-value
requirements.canonical: A specific value IS the basic matching mechanism of TTCN-3 templates.
requirements.original: Specific values are the basic matching mechanism of TTCN-3 templates.

requirements.subject: ent:specific-value
requirements.canonical: A specific value in a template IS an expression that does not contain any matching mechanism.
requirements.original: Specific values in templates are expressions which do not contain any matching mechanisms.

requirements.subject: ent:specific-value
requirements.canonical: A specific value matching mechanism has the syntax SingleExpression.
requirements.original: SingleExpression

requirements.subject: ent:specific-value
requirements.canonical: The specific value matching mechanism IS an expression that evaluates to a specific value.
requirements.original: The matching mechanism for a specific value is an expression that evaluates to a specific value.
